mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns when UNRATE is below 6%, or the mechanism's IC is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.15% indicates monetary tightening, which may lead to decreased borrowing and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.15%, or the mechanism's IC is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in both consumer and housing markets, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns when both RSAFS and HOUST increase, or the mechanism's IC is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic activity and supply, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns when INDPRO increases, or the mechanism's IC is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns when GDPC1 increases, or the mechanism's IC is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns when PAYEMS increases by more than 100,000, or the mechanism's IC is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market and potential monetary policy constraints, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or the mechanism's IC is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns when HOUST increases, or the mechanism's IC is below 0.03 in out-of-sample testing.
